nodes.description: Hypoplastic or absent finger flexion creases, a major diagnostic criterion.

evidence.reference_title: Sheldon-Hall syndrome.
evidence.snippet: The major diagnostic criteria for SHS are ulnar deviation, camptodactyly, overriding fingers, hypoplastic and/or absent flexion creases, talipes equinovarus, calcaneovalgus abnormalities, vertical talus and/or metatarsus varus

evidence.reference_title: Sheldon-Hall syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Contractures of the upper limbs typically manifest as overlapping fingers, camptodactyly, and ulnar deviation.

nodes.description: Fixed contractures of the distal limb joints that form in utero, are most severe at birth, and improve or remain stable postnatally rather than progressing; flexion contractures can worsen without therapy.

evidence.reference_title: Sheldon-Hall syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Contractures are most severe at birth and non-progressive. However, flexion contractures can worsen over time in the absence of appropriate intervention (e.g., occupational therapy, physical therapy, surgery).

evidence.reference_title: A gain-of-function mutation in Tnni2 impeded bone development through increasing Hif3a expression in DA2B mice.
evidence.snippet: Like DA2B patients, homozygous and heterozygous mutant mice exhibited an obviously smaller body size than their wild-type counterparts (Figure 1B and Figure S2B), as well as forelimb contracture (Figure S2A and C), supporting the idea that the mutation has a dominant effect

nodes.description: Multiple congenital contractures predominantly of the hands and feet, present at birth, without primary neurological disease.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation in the fast skeletal muscle troponin I gene causes myopathy and distal arthrogryposis.
evidence.snippet: The five affected individuals had predominantly distal congenital joint contractures, mild facial involvement (mild micrognathia, narrow palpebral fissures), and no detectable muscle weakness.

evidence.reference_title: A mutation in the fast skeletal muscle troponin I gene causes myopathy and distal arthrogryposis.
evidence.snippet: The four affected adults had slightly increased levels of creatine kinase in blood, and muscle biopsy specimens showed findings of myopathy with changes restricted to type 2 fibers.

nodes.description: In Tnni2 K175del knock-in mice, Tnni2 was expressed in growth-plate osteoblasts and chondrocytes, mutant protein transactivated Hif3a more than wild type, and increased Hif3a with reduced Vegf was associated with delayed endochondral ossification and small body size. This is a mouse-only proposal for the short stature of DA2B; it has not been examined in patients.

evidence.reference_title: A gain-of-function mutation in Tnni2 impeded bone development through increasing Hif3a expression in DA2B mice.
evidence.snippet: The increased amount of hif3a resulted in impairment of angiogenesis, delay in endochondral ossification, and decrease in chondrocyte differentiation and osteoblast proliferation, suggesting that hif3a counteracted hif1a-induced Vegf expression in DA2B mice.

nodes.description: Thin filaments carrying DA-associated troponin I mutants activate myosin ATPase more at every Ca2+ concentration, and troponin-exchanged skinned fast-twitch fibers show increased Ca2+ sensitivity of force. nodes.description: Proposed consequence of the Ca2+-sensitization: excess contractile activity of fast-twitch muscle during fetal development. This node is an inference from isolated-fiber and reconstituted-protein data; it has not been measured in patient myofibers or in fetal muscle.

evidence.snippet: There is no specific therapy for SHS. However, patients benefit from early intervention with occupational and physical therapy, serial casting, and/or surgery.

evidence.snippet: Other common clinical features of SHS include prominent nasolabial folds, high arched palate, attached earlobes, mild cervical webbing, short stature, severe camptodactyly, ulnar deviation, and vertical talus and/or talipes equinovarus.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in genes encoding fast-twitch contractile proteins cause distal arthrogryposis syndromes.
evidence.snippet: We now report that DA2B is caused by mutations in TNNI2 that are predicted to disrupt the carboxy-terminal domain of an isoform of troponin I (TnI) specific to the troponin-tropomyosin (Tc-Tm) complex of fast-twitch myofibers.

evidence.reference_title: Spectrum of mutations that cause distal arthrogryposis types 1 and 2B.
evidence.snippet: Disease-causing mutations in 56/153 (37%) kindreds including 14/48 (29%) with DA1 and 42/105 (40%) with DA2B were distributed nearly equally across TNNI2, TNNT3, TPM2, and MYH3.

nodes.description: Heterozygous TNNI2 variants alter the carboxy-terminal region of fast skeletal troponin I, the region required for its inhibitory action. Troponin I binds actin and tropomyosin and, in the absence of Ca2+, prevents contraction; the variants are predicted to disrupt this regulatory interaction rather than abolish the protein.

nodes.description: Knock-in of the human DA2B K175del allele into mouse Tnni2. Heterozygous and homozygous mice show forelimb contracture and small body size.

In one TNNI2 (K176del) family, adult carriers had mildly raised creatine kinase and biopsy myopathic changes confined to type 2 fibers, without clinical weakness. The family was classified DA1, so this node rests on one family at the DA1 end of the TNNI2 spectrum.
